title: Linux: after the running termal binary is replaced on disk, new sessions get TERMAL_CLI/MCP command "<path> (deleted)" and lose the TermAl MCP tools
outcome: Linux: after the running termal binary is replaced on disk, new sessions get TERMAL_CLI/MCP command "<path> (deleted)" and lose the TermAl MCP tools
acceptance: On Linux, when the running host's executable file has been replaced on disk (the landing install puts a new build at target/release/termal while the host keeps running until a restart), sessions started afterwards still get a working TermAl delegation MCP server and a TERMAL_CLI that runs: the host never hands out a command path ending in ' (deleted)'. The fix uses the host's own executable in a way that survives replacement (for example the path captured at startup or /proc/self/exe as an executable handle), with no new condition.

A test reproduces the replacement on Linux (or exercises the path-resolution seam with a ' (deleted)' current_exe value) and shows the session's MCP command and TERMAL_CLI resolve to a runnable executable.
The cause is recorded on this item from the code and the test.
